req.title: Delete only by author
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden when a user attempts to delete a post they did not author.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that only the author of a post may delete it; any other authenticated user must receive HTTP 403. Three test cases are designed: (1) Positive – the actual author (user 'test', id=1) deletes post id=1 and receives a 2xx/redirect response; (2) Negative – a different authenticated user ('other', id=2) attempts to delete post id=1 and must receive exactly HTTP 403; (3) Boundary – an unauthenticated (anonymous) client attempts to delete post id=1 and must be redirected to login (302), confirming the login_required guard fires before the authz check. Together these cover the EP partition of author vs non-author, the NEG path for the 403 branch, and the STC state of unauthenticated→login redirect as a boundary state transition. Exact status codes are asserted to kill comparison-operator and constant mutations.

tests.name: test_author_can_delete_own_post
preconditions: Database contains post id=1 authored by user id=1 (username='test')
User 'test' is authenticated in the session
expected: HTTP 302 redirect (successful delete redirects to index)
trace: R-FLASKR-020: author is permitted; delete succeeds with redirect
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_author_can_delete_own_post():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/1/delete')
    assert r.status_code == 302
    assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

test_author_can_delete_own_post()

import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

def test_non_author_delete_does_not_delete_post():
    fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
    os.close(fd)
    app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
    with app.app_context():
        from flaskr.db import init_db
        init_db()
    client = app.test_client()
    r = client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'other', 'password': 'other'})
    assert r.status_code == 302
    r = client.post('/1/delete')
